label: Norwegian Red

names.text: Other names are listed in the Wikipedia article's opening, read on WebFetch: Norsk Rødt Fe, Norsk Raudt Fe, Norwegian Dairy Cattle and Norwegian Red Cattle.

about.text: Norway's main dairy breed, formed by merging traditional regional breeds. It is reared principally for milk, and in 2016 it made up about 85% of Norway's cattle. It has been exported to many countries, including Madagascar.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: a Norwegian breed of dairy cattle reared principally for milk; about 85% of Norway's cattle in 2016; exports including Madagascar, Argentina, the Netherlands, Australia, Ireland, New Zealand and the United States.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: formed in 1961 through successive mergers of various traditional and regional breeds.

Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "The average annual yield is 7125 kg per cow." The page gives no year for this figure, so none is recorded. Lactation length and per-lactation yield are not given on the page.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "Milk fat: 4.24% on average." The page gives no protein figure.
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: dairy only, "reared principally for milk".
Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: FAO (2007) "not at risk".

facts.v: Exports to Madagascar began in the 1960s, and Madagascar had over 50,000 head by 2003.

sources.text: Wikipedia article, read on WebFetch: "Madagascar, where exports began in the 1960s, had over 50,000 head by 2003."

gaps: No national head count for Norway was found. A 2013 presentation (WebSearch text only, source not opened) gave about 240,000 cows in the recording system, but I did not open it, so it is left out. Geno's current figures were not reached. Protein, lactation length and per-lactation yield are not on the Wikipedia page. The 6,200 L figure from a mirror site is unverified and left out.
